name: citedevidence
description: Search 250 million scholarly papers, check and format references, and run Deep Research and manuscript reviews with your CitedEvidence account.

interface.longDescription:
CitedEvidence gives ChatGPT and Codex access to CitedEvidence Scholar, a database of over 250 million scholarly works, and to your CitedEvidence research account.

- Find real papers on any topic, follow who cites what, and look up researchers, so answers rest on papers that exist.
- Check reference lists: each entry is matched by DOI, title, year and author and marked verified, wrong or not found.
- Format references in APA, MLA, Chicago, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver, AMA or Nature, with BibTeX.
- Save papers to your CitedEvidence Library, with the free full text when available.
- Start a cited Deep Research report or a specialist manuscript review and follow progress in the chat.

For students, researchers and academic writers. Requires a CitedEvidence account (free to create). Searching, checking, formatting and saving are free; Deep Research and manuscript reviews use credits from your CitedEvidence account at the same rates as on citedevidence.com. Nothing can be bought inside ChatGPT. Coverage follows CitedEvidence Scholar: very new papers and some conference proceedings may be missing.
defaultPrompt: Find highly cited papers since 2018 on sleep deprivation and working memory.
Check these references and tell me which ones are wrong.

positive.description: Finds real papers on a topic with year filtering and shows the paper card.
positive.prompt: Find highly cited papers since 2018 on sleep deprivation and working memory.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_papers with year_from 2018 (and most_cited sort or similar), shows a card of real papers with authors, year, venue and DOI, and summarises them citing only returned papers.

positive.description: Flags invented and mismatched references in a list.
positive.prompt: Check whether these references are real: (1) Lim, J., & Dinges, D. F. (2010). A meta-analysis of the impact of short-term sleep deprivation on cognitive variables. Psychological Bulletin, 136(3), 375-389. (2) Smith, J. (2019). Quantum gravitational effects on medieval bread fermentation. Journal of Imaginary Studies, 12(3), 45-67.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls verify_references; reports reference 1 as verified with DOI 10.1037/a0018883 and reference 2 as not found, and offers corrections.

positive.description: Formats references from DOIs in a requested style.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls format_citations with style apa and returns two APA 7 references (LeCun et al., 2015, Nature; Lim & Dinges, 2010, Psychological Bulletin) with in-text citations; the card offers style switching and copy.

positive.description: Follows the citation graph from a paper.
positive.prompt: Which papers cite W2173737475? Show five relevant ones.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls find_related_papers with relation cited_by and limit 5 and lists five citing papers with years and DOIs.

positive.description: Starts Deep Research and reports progress.
positive.prompt: Run Deep Research on whether community health workers improve blood pressure control in sub-Saharan Africa.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls start_research, tells the user it takes a few minutes and uses credits, shows a progress card; a later get_research returns the finished cited report and a link to it.

negative.prompt: Write a haiku about autumn leaves.
Book me a flight from Kampala to Nairobi next Friday.

publication.release_notes: First release: paper search, reference checking, citation formatting, Library saving, Deep Research and manuscript review.
